P0700.title: Transmission Control System (MIL Request)
P0700.description: P0700 is a notice code: the separate transmission control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault – a sensor, solenoid, ratio or speed sensor code – is stored in the transmission module and must be read with a tool that can address it; simple OBD readers often show only P0700. GM's engine module reads the request message from 3 s after start; Subaru-based systems (Saab 9-2X) light the MIL at once and clear it after three fault-free cycles. Ford's engine modules with integrated transmission control do not use P0700. Any limp mode comes from the transmission fault, not from P0700.

causes.label: Actual fault stored in the transmission module (sensor, solenoid, ratio, speed sensor)
Wrong transmission fluid level or condition causing slip or ratio codes
Harness or connector at the transmission corroded or damaged
Low system voltage or weak battery
Transmission module or software faulty

symptoms: Check engine light, possibly transmission warning
Depending on the transmission fault: limp mode, harsh or delayed shifts
Often no symptoms if the fault was intermittent
Simple OBD reader shows only P0700

P0701.title: Transmission Control System Range/Performance
P0701.description: P0701 means the transmission control system works outside its expected range or its function is implausible – without a circuit fault. What exactly is checked is up to the manufacturer; no GM, Ford, Saab or bulletin document available to us describes the strategy. The only manufacturer evidence is Ford's engine module list for 6.8 L E- and F-Series trucks, where P0701 is stored without the check engine light. Typically the control cannot plausibly achieve the requested gear, pressure or torque, and the transmission goes into limp mode. Individual components have their own codes (P0705 ff range sensor, P0715 ff speed sensors, P0750 ff solenoids).

causes.label: Transmission control faulty internally or software
Implausible input signals (speed or range sensor) without own circuit fault
Wrong fluid level or quality – hydraulics do not respond
Harness or connector with contact resistance

symptoms: Transmission warning (at Ford no check engine light)
Limp mode with fixed gear or missing gears
Harsh or irregular shifts

P0702.title: Transmission Control System Electrical
P0702.description: P0702 reports an electrical fault in the transmission control system as a whole – typically the supply of the transmission actuators (solenoid supply, transmission relay, supply switch in the module) or a circuit fault not assigned to a single component. No manufacturer document available to us describes it in detail; Ford's engine module list for 6.8 L E- and F-Series trucks stores it without the check engine light. If the solenoid supply is lost, transmissions usually fall back to a hydraulic limp gear. Individual solenoids have their own codes (P0750 ff); actuator supply is P0657 ff.

causes.label: Transmission actuator supply interrupted (fuse, relay, ground)
Harness or connector at transmission or module damaged, corroded or oil-soaked
Transmission module output stage or supply switch faulty
Low or fluctuating system voltage

symptoms: Transmission limp mode with fixed gear
Transmission warning; check engine light depending on the maker
No or harsh shifts, further solenoid codes

P0703.title: Brake Switch B Circuit
P0703.description: Brake switch A is usually the brake light switch, B a second, redundant contact or signal used to cancel cruise control, release the converter clutch, check 'brake before throttle' and for stop-start. Since about 2014 GM receives it as a CAN message from the body module and checks its integrity (rolling counter, protection value: 3 of 10 faulty in 2014, 9 of 17 in 2025) without the check engine light; cruise control is disabled. Subaru-based systems (Saab 9-2X) check the circuit electrically during stops and starts and light the MIL after two trips. An NHTSA investigation of Hyundai and Kia brake light switches lists P0703 with a brake light that stays on. Brake switch A codes are P0571–P0573, disagreement between A and B is P0504.

causes.label: Brake light or double switch worn, corroded or misadjusted
Wiring or connector at the pedal damaged, fuse blown
CAN message from the body module disturbed (GM: software, bus fault)
Aftermarket LED lamps or trailer module distorting the circuit

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be engaged or drops out
Brake light stays on or does not work
Selector cannot be moved out of P (shift lock)
Check engine light depending on the maker

P0704.title: Clutch Switch Input Circuit
P0704.description: Only on cars with a clutch pedal: the clutch switch tells the engine module that the clutch is depressed, used to cancel cruise control, smooth load changes when shifting and for stop-start. The check is a plausibility test over driving events rather than a voltage check: Saab's Trionic T8 expects a change of state every time the car pulls away from 3 to 50 km/h (four misses in a row), the EDC16 diesel at gear changes (25 in a row, above 35 km/h and 1500 rpm), and Ford compares its two clutch switches continuously. None of them lights the check engine light; cruise control is disabled. Separate clutch pedal switch codes are P0830–P0835.

causes.label: Clutch switch faulty or misadjusted (does not switch or too late)
Connector or wiring at the pedal box damaged or corroded
Floor mat or pedal stop shifted, switch bracket broken
Driving style (pulling away or shifting without fully depressing the clutch)

symptoms: Cruise control not working or not cancelling when declutching
Jerks or rev hang when shifting
Stop-start inactive
Usually no check engine light

P0705.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit (PRNDL Input)
P0705.description: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805). P0705 is the circuit or pattern fault: the module receives a combination that matches no valid position. Ford flags an invalid pattern after 5 s (digital sensor) or 200 ms (4-bit sensor), checking continuously with the check engine light; Saab's 9-5 (9600) detects an impossible combination of its four contacts and goes into limp mode with the gearbox warning. The transmission no longer knows the range reliably – limp mode, start interlock or reversing light may be affected. Check the harness for shorts to ground before replacing the sensor.

causes.label: Range sensor worn, dirty or with oil or water ingress
Sensor misadjusted or selector cable out of adjustment
Harness or connector at the transmission damaged, short to ground
Transmission or engine module input faulty

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Transmission limp mode, fixed gear, harsh shifts
Starting problems in P/N or start interlock
Wrong gear indication, reversing light not working

P0706.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0706.description: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805). P0706 means the signal is present but implausible. Ford uses it per transmission: for its PWM sensor when the frequency leaves 100–175 Hz (nominal 125 Hz), for the 6F digital sensor when it stays in the transition zone between two positions. Saab's 9-5 (9650), whose sensor sits in the transmission module, flags a sum of the two opposing channels more than 0.29 V away from 5 V, with the lamp in the first trip; adaptations are frozen, the gearbox holds 2nd gear in D and the engine may not restart after switch-off.

causes.label: Range sensor or transmission module with integrated sensor faulty
Selector cable or sensor misadjusted (position between two ranges)
Contact resistance in sensor supply or ground
Moisture or oil in harness or connector

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Transmission limp mode, fixed gear, harsh shifts
Starting problems in P/N or start interlock
Wrong gear indication, reversing light not working

P0707.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Low
P0707.description: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805). P0707 means the sensor A signal is too low – usually a short to ground or lost supply. GM's T87A transmission module flags a PWM duty cycle below 8.8 % for 0.5 s within 1.5 s, with the lamp in the first trip; Ford flags a duty cycle below 10 %, an analog sensor below 0.2 V for 5 s or a dual-analog channel below 0.127 V for 200 ms; Saab's 9-5 (9650) below 0.127 V for 100 ms twice. 'Low' refers to the signal, not to a gear.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground (chafing at the transmission case)
Sensor faulty internally
Sensor supply missing (5 V reference, fuse)
Connector corroded or oil in the connector

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Transmission limp mode, fixed gear, harsh shifts
Starting problems in P/N or start interlock
Wrong gear indication, reversing light not working

P0708.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit High
P0708.description: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805). P0708 means the sensor A signal is too high – a short to voltage or, depending on the circuit, an open line pulled up. GM's T87A transmission module flags a PWM duty cycle above 91.2 % for 1.8 s within 2.25 s, lamp in the first trip; Ford flags a duty cycle above 90 %, an analog sensor above 4.8 V for 5 s, a dual-analog channel above 4.84 V for 200 ms, and explicitly an open circuit on its digital sensor (all switches open, e.g. unplugged); Saab's 9-5 (9650) above 4.87 V for 100 ms twice, with 2nd gear held and a restart interlock.

causes.label: Sensor connector off or signal/ground wire open
Signal wire shorted to voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Poor sensor or transmission ground

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Transmission limp mode, fixed gear, harsh shifts
Starting problems in P/N or start interlock
Wrong gear indication, reversing light not working

P0709.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0709.description: The transmission range sensor (selector or multifunction switch, PRNDL) reports the selected range; it may be a multi-contact switch with a bit pattern per position, an analog sensor with two opposing voltages adding up to 5 V, or a contactless PWM sensor. Its second channel has its own codes (P2801–P2805). P0709 means the sensor A signal jumps briefly to invalid values or drops out without being permanently low or high. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0709 – Ford catches short invalid states under P0705 and P0706 instead – so the description follows the sibling codes. Sliding contacts in older selector switches are a typical source; the transmission may briefly lose the range and go into limp mode.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion in the range sensor connector
Worn sliding contacts in the selector switch
Harness chafing on transmission or bracket, breaking when moved
Misadjusted sensor or selector cable (position at the limit)

symptoms: Intermittent transmission warning or check engine light
Gear indication flickers, brief shift jolts
Occasional starting problems in P/N
Occasional limp mode

P070A.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit
P070A.description: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump (capacitive or voltage-based) report the oil level to the transmission module; measurements are only valid under defined conditions – an Allison patent names fluid temperature, vehicle at rest, low input speed and a tilt correction. Such sensors are mainly found in heavy automatic transmissions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P070A is the general circuit fault of this sensor (open or fault in the signal circuit). Because the oil level does not usually affect emissions directly, a rating without the check engine light is likely; expect a transmission warning or a missing level display. An actually low oil level is not a P070A fault. Range, low, high and intermittent are P070B–P070E; fluid temperature has its own codes (P0710 ff).

causes.label: Fluid level sensor faulty
Wire or connector to the sensor (often through the sump or transmission connector) open or oil-soaked
Transmission module input faulty

symptoms: Transmission warning or 'check fluid level' message
Fluid level display missing
Usually no driveability problems

P070B.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P070B.description: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump (capacitive or voltage-based) report the oil level to the transmission module; measurements are only valid under defined conditions – an Allison patent names fluid temperature, vehicle at rest, low input speed and a tilt correction. Such sensors are mainly found in heavy automatic transmissions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P070B means the signal is present but implausible – it does not change, does not fit temperature or operating state, or lies outside the physically possible range. Such checks only make sense within the valid measuring window. A truly wrong oil level (overfilled, underfilled) or the wrong fluid can also appear as an implausible signal. The circuit fault is P070A.

causes.label: Fluid level sensor drifting or dirty (wear debris, sludge)
Fluid level actually wrong (over- or underfilled) or wrong fluid
Contact resistance in connector or wire
Faulty tilt or temperature compensation (fluid temperature sensor fault)

symptoms: Warning or message about transmission fluid level
Fluid level display implausible or unavailable
Usually no driveability problems

P070C.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit Low
P070C.description: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump report the oil level to the transmission module as a voltage; an Allison patent converts it to millimetres and only accepts readings with the vehicle at rest, warm fluid, low input speed and a tilt correction. Such sensors are mainly found in heavy automatic transmissions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P070C means the sensor signal is below its lower limit – typically the signal wire shorted to ground or a sensor shorted internally. Because the oil level does not usually affect emissions directly, a rating without the check engine light is likely; expect a transmission warning or a missing level display. An actually low oil level is P070F.

causes.label: Signal wire to the level sensor shorted to ground (chafing, transmission connector)
Level sensor faulty internally
Transmission connector soaked in oil or corroded
Module input faulty

symptoms: Fluid level display missing or warning to check transmission fluid
Usually no driveability problems
Transmission warning lamp depending on manufacturer

P070D.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit High
P070D.description: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump report the oil level to the transmission module as a voltage; an Allison patent converts it to millimetres and only accepts readings with the vehicle at rest, warm fluid, low input speed and a tilt correction. Such sensors are mainly found in heavy automatic transmissions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P070D means the sensor signal is above its upper limit – typically an open signal or ground wire, pulled up inside the module, or a short to positive. Because the oil level does not usually affect emissions directly, a rating without the check engine light is likely; expect a transmission warning or a missing level display. The opposite fault is P070C.

causes.label: Wire or connector to the level sensor open
Sensor faulty (open)
Signal wire shorted to positive
Control module faulty

symptoms: Fluid level display missing or warning to check transmission fluid
Usually no driveability problems
Transmission warning lamp depending on manufacturer

P070E.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P070E.description: Fluid level sensors in the transmission sump report the oil level to the transmission module as a voltage; an Allison patent converts it to millimetres and only accepts readings with the vehicle at rest, warm fluid, low input speed and a tilt correction. Such sensors are mainly found in heavy automatic transmissions. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. P070E means the level signal drops out briefly or jumps unrealistically – usually a loose contact or a wire breaking under movement. Sloshing and tilt also make readings vary, which is why valid measurements need the vehicle at rest. Because the oil level does not usually affect emissions directly, a rating without the check engine light is likely; expect a transmission warning or a missing level display.

causes.label: Loose contact in transmission connector or harness
Sensor with internal contact fault
Contaminated or foaming fluid at the sensor

symptoms: Fluid level display jumps or drops out at times
Intermittent warning message

P070F.title: Transmission Fluid Level Too Low
P070F.description: P070F is not a circuit fault but a condition: a working fluid level sensor reports a level below the target band. In the Allison patent the module compares the measured height in millimetres with a tilt-dependent band and reports at least a quart too little or too much – only with the vehicle at rest, fluid above about 30–40 °C and low input speed. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code. Take it seriously: real fluid loss leads to slipping, overheating (P0218) and ratio errors. Leaks at the pan gasket, seals or cooler lines and wrong filling after service are the usual causes.

causes.label: Leak (pan gasket, shaft seals, cooler lines)
Underfilled after fluid change or repair
Level sensor reading wrong (drift)

symptoms: Warning: transmission fluid level low
Slipping gears, delayed engagement
Transmission overheating
Oil spots under the vehicle

P0710.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0710.description: The transmission fluid temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as the fluid warms; the module feeds it with 5 V through a resistor. A low signal therefore means very hot or a short to ground, a high signal very cold or an open circuit. P0710 is the general circuit code used when a manufacturer does not separate low and high. Subaru-based systems (Saab 9-2X) flag 0.1 V or less or 4.7 V or more, light the MIL after two consecutive trips and use 80 °C as substitute. Ford's 2023 diesels use P0710 alongside P0712/P0713 for open and short circuits, without MIL, after 5–12 s, substituting coolant temperature. GM uses only the split codes. With the substitute value the shift quality suffers: harsh shifts and a late converter clutch.

causes.label: Fluid temperature sensor faulty (often part of the internal harness or valve body)
Transmission connector leaking or corroded, oil in the connector
Wire open or shorted
Transmission or engine module faulty

symptoms: Harsh or late shifts
Torque converter clutch applies late or not at all
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer
Implausible fluid temperature in the scan tool

P0711.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0711.description: P0711 means the fluid temperature signal is electrically valid but implausible. Manufacturers check three things: the fluid does not warm up as expected (GM 2025 still below 15 °C after the calibrated warm-up time, Saab's AF40 below 20 °C after 10 minutes of driving), the value is stuck (Ford: within ±2 °F for about 2.5 minutes below 70 or above 225 °F), or it jumps unrealistically. GM's 6T70 compares it with the module's internal temperature. The MIL rating varies: GM's newer modules after two trips, Saab AF40 none, Ford none; a 2013 Ram 6.7 bulletin moved P0711–P0714 from one to two trips. A substitute value then limits adaption and converter clutch control.

causes.label: Fluid temperature sensor drifting or stuck
High contact resistance in connector or harness (oil, corrosion)
Very cold weather or short trips (fluid does not reach warm-up threshold)
Outdated module software
Fluid cooler thermostat faulty

symptoms: Harsh or late shifts
Torque converter clutch applies late or not at all
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer
Implausible fluid temperature in the scan tool

P0712.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0712.description: The transmission fluid temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as the fluid warms; the module feeds it with 5 V through a resistor. A low signal therefore means very hot or a short to ground, a high signal very cold or an open circuit. P0712 means the signal is too low – the sensor reads extremely hot, or the signal wire is shorted to ground. GM's 2025 transmission modules flag below 13.5 Ω for 5 of 6 s after two trips; the 2018 LT4 engine module below 17.88 Ω (over 150 °C) without MIL; the 2007 Allison 1000 150 °C or more for 2.5 s; Saab's AF40 over 200 °C; Ford below 0.05 V for 5–12 s without MIL. The module substitutes a value (coolant temperature, 80 °C or a hot mode) and may shift with hot-fluid strategy. Real overheating with a good sensor is P0218.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground (internal harness, chafing)
Sensor shorted internally
Transmission actually severely overheated
Control module faulty

symptoms: Transmission in hot mode (early converter clutch, changed shift points)
Harsh shifts
Extremely high fluid temperature shown
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer

P0713.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0713.description: The transmission fluid temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as the fluid warms; the module feeds it with 5 V through a resistor. A low signal therefore means very hot or a short to ground, a high signal very cold or an open circuit. P0713 means the signal is too high – the sensor reads extremely cold, or the circuit is open or shorted to positive. GM's 2025 modules flag above 284 kΩ for 5 of 6 s after two trips; the 2007 Allison 1000 −45 °C or below for 2.5 s; Saab's AF40 below −43 °C; Ford above 4.6 V for 5–12 s without MIL. Many require prior running time or a warm engine so a genuine −40 °C cold start does not count (Allison: coolant above 20 °C; Saab: over 10 minutes of driving). The transmission then stays in its cold strategy: open converter clutch, late upshifts.

causes.label: Transmission connector loose or corroded, wire open
Sensor open internally
Signal wire shorted to positive
Control module faulty

symptoms: Fluid temperature shown around −40 °C
Converter clutch stays open, late upshifts
Higher fuel consumption
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer

P0714.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0714.description: The transmission fluid temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as the fluid warms; the module feeds it with 5 V through a resistor. A low signal therefore means very hot or a short to ground, a high signal very cold or an open circuit. P0714 means the signal drops out or jumps briefly – not long enough for P0712 or P0713. Ford's 2012 6R80 transmission names P0714 among its fluid temperature checks for open, short and in-range faults. Ram 6.7 bulletins of 2013 changed P0711–P0714 from a one-trip to a two-trip MIL to avoid needless warnings. GM files such jumps under P0711 instead. No source publishes thresholds for P0714 itself. A loose contact in the transmission connector or a chafing internal harness is the usual cause.

causes.label: Loose contact in transmission connector (oil, corrosion, spread pins)
Internal harness chafing from movement or vibration
Sensor with internal contact fault
Module software (false warning)

symptoms: Harsh shifts at times
Jumping fluid temperature display
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer

P0715.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0715.description: The input or turbine shaft speed sensor – a Hall sensor with square-wave output or an inductive sensor with sine output – reports the speed behind the torque converter. With output and engine speed it gives the actual gear ratio, converter slip and shift timing. P0715 is the general circuit code. Ford uses it for 'no signal' too: the vehicle is moving under power (engine above converter stall speed, output speed plausible) but the sensor reports under 200 rpm for 5–30 s; Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch sets it for a hardware-detected fault of input shaft sensor 1. Subaru-based systems flag an open or shorted circuit, Saab's Aisin box no input signal while the output sensor works, substituting output speed. GM does not use P0715. Limp mode, harsh shifts and a disabled converter clutch follow.

causes.label: Speed sensor faulty (Hall IC or coil open or shorted)
Connector or harness corroded, chafed or loose pins (with internal sensors also the pass-through connector)
Metal debris on the sensor magnet or damaged reluctor wheel
Transmission module or its sensor supply faulty

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode with fixed gear, harsh shifts
Torque converter clutch does not apply
Input speed shows 0 or implausible in the scan tool

P0716.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0716.description: The input or turbine shaft speed sensor – a Hall sensor with square-wave output or an inductive sensor with sine output – reports the speed behind the torque converter. With output and engine speed it gives the actual gear ratio, converter slip and shift timing. P0716 means a signal is present but implausible: too high, or dropping suddenly without recovering. GM's 2025 modules count drops of more than 650 rpm between 25 ms samples and fail after more than three; the 6T70 in the Saab 9-4X flags a 1350 rpm drop for 1 s; the 2007 Allison 1000 also detects noise and swapped sensor wires; all after one trip. Ford's 6R80 flags turbine speed above 7700 rpm. The 6T70 then runs only reverse and fifth gear, with maximum line pressure and no converter clutch.

causes.label: Loose contact or chafing in the sensor circuit
Sensor faulty, wrong air gap or metal debris
Reluctor wheel or clutch drum damaged
Sensor wires swapped after repair or interference

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode with fixed gear (6T70: reverse and fifth only)
Harsh or delayed shifts
Torque converter clutch locked out

P0717.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
P0717.description: The input or turbine shaft speed sensor – a Hall sensor with square-wave output or an inductive sensor with sine output – reports the speed behind the torque converter. With output and engine speed it gives the actual gear ratio, converter slip and shift timing. P0717 means there is practically no input speed signal although the vehicle is driving under power. GM's 2025 modules flag under 200 rpm for more than 4 s with torque applied, the 6T70 under 50 rpm for 5 s, the Allison 1000 under 61 rpm with output above 500 rpm; Ford under 200 rpm for 5–30 s; all after one trip. GM calls it 'circuit low voltage', but means missing frequency. On GM's 10-speed both input and output sensors share a supply – P0717 together with P0722 points to that supply rather than two sensors.

causes.label: Speed sensor faulty (Hall IC or coil open or shorted)
Connector or harness corroded, chafed or loose pins (with internal sensors also the pass-through connector)
Metal debris on the sensor magnet or damaged reluctor wheel
Transmission module or its sensor supply faulty

symptoms: Check engine and/or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode with fixed gear, harsh shifts
Torque converter clutch does not apply
Input speed shows 0 or implausible in the scan tool

P0718.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0718.description: The input or turbine shaft speed sensor – a Hall sensor with square-wave output or an inductive sensor with sine output – reports the speed behind the torque converter. With output and engine speed it gives the actual gear ratio, converter slip and shift timing. P0718 means the signal is present but jumps or drops out briefly. Ford's petrol modules from 2012 to 2023 count 200 turbine speed spikes above 400 rpm with at most 1.5 s between them in a forward gear. GM's Honda-built five-speed of 2006 flags jumps of more than 3 mph per 10 ms three times in 500 ms, after two trips; GM's own transmissions file such jumps under P0716 instead. Loose contacts and electrical interference are the usual causes; shifts become erratic and limp mode may follow at times.

causes.label: Loose contact, corroded connector or chafing
Electrical interference (shielding, ground, added consumers)
Metal debris on the sensor or loose mounting
Sensor faulty internally (temperature-dependent)

symptoms: Occasional harsh or unexpected shifts
Warning lamp
Converter clutch applies and releases unevenly
Limp mode at times

P0719.title: Brake Switch B Circuit Low
P0719.description: Brake switch B is the brake signal to the transmission module or a second brake switch channel, used to release the converter clutch, adapt shift strategy on grades and cancel cruise control. Low and high describe the signal voltage, and what that means depends on polarity: GM's converter clutch brake switch is closed at rest (12 V), while Saab's Trionic 8 sees 12 V when braking. Detection is always a plausibility check against driving: the brake reads applied during accelerations or never applied during decelerations. P0719 means the signal stays low. For GM that reads as brake applied: 2006 transmission modules flag it after eight accelerations without the brake releasing, without MIL. Saab's Trionic 8 flags the brake light signal not changing during four decelerations from 40 to 3 km/h and disables cruise control. The opposite is P0724.

causes.label: Brake light switch faulty or misadjusted
Wire to the module open (GM) or shorted to ground (Saab T8)
Connector at the pedal box corroded
Brake light circuit fuse blown

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be activated or switches off
Unusual shifting, converter clutch behaviour changed
No downshift on uphill grades (Subaru)
Brake lights stay off or on

P071A.title: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit
P071A.description: A transmission mode switch selects an alternative shift schedule such as sport, winter or tow/haul; J2012 does not define which button is A or B. No manufacturer document available to us uses P071A–P071F: GM monitors its analog drive mode switch under its own codes (low below 21–29 % of 5 V, high from 94 %, 200 of 250 samples, two trips), which shows how such buttons are read as coded voltages. P071A is the general circuit fault of mode switch A: its state is invalid or implausible. The transmission then usually stays on its normal schedule. Low and high are P071B/P071C, switch B has P071D–P071F; the range sensor (PRNDL) is P0705 ff.

causes.label: Mode switch A faulty (selector lever or console)
Wiring or connector in the console damaged (spilled drinks, chafing)
Resistor coding drifted (analog buttons)
Control module faulty

symptoms: Mode A cannot be selected or stays active
Mode indicator missing or flashing
Transmission stays on the normal shift schedule

P071B.title: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit Low
P071B.description: A transmission mode switch selects an alternative shift schedule such as sport, winter or tow/haul; J2012 does not define which button is A or B. No manufacturer document available to us uses P071A–P071F: GM monitors its analog drive mode switch under its own codes (low below 21–29 % of 5 V, high from 94 %, 200 of 250 samples, two trips), which shows how such buttons are read as coded voltages. P071B means the signal of mode switch A is below its lower limit: with analog, resistor-coded buttons a short to ground, with digital buttons switching to ground a button stuck pressed. The opposite is P071C.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Button stuck pressed (switching to ground)
Moisture or dirt in the button
Control module faulty

symptoms: Mode A cannot be selected or stays active
Mode indicator missing or flashing
Transmission stays on the normal shift schedule

P071C.title: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit High
P071C.description: A transmission mode switch selects an alternative shift schedule such as sport, winter or tow/haul; J2012 does not define which button is A or B. No manufacturer document available to us uses P071A–P071F: GM monitors its analog drive mode switch under its own codes (low below 21–29 % of 5 V, high from 94 %, 200 of 250 samples, two trips), which shows how such buttons are read as coded voltages. P071C means the signal of mode switch A is above its upper limit – typically an open circuit pulled up inside the module, or a short to positive. The mode then cannot be selected. The opposite is P071B.

causes.label: Wire or connector to the button open
Button open internally
Signal wire shorted to positive

symptoms: Mode A cannot be selected or stays active
Mode indicator missing or flashing
Transmission stays on the normal shift schedule

P071D.title: Transmission Mode Switch B Circuit
P071D.description: A transmission mode switch selects an alternative shift schedule such as sport, winter or tow/haul; J2012 does not define which button is A or B. No manufacturer document available to us uses P071A–P071F: GM monitors its analog drive mode switch under its own codes (low below 21–29 % of 5 V, high from 94 %, 200 of 250 samples, two trips), which shows how such buttons are read as coded voltages. Low and high are P071E/P071F; switch A has P071A–P071C.

causes.label: Mode switch B faulty (selector lever or console)
Wiring or connector in the console damaged (spilled drinks, chafing)
Resistor coding drifted (analog buttons)
Control module faulty

symptoms: Mode B cannot be selected or stays active
Mode indicator missing or flashing
Transmission stays on the normal shift schedule

P0720.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit
P0720.description: The output shaft speed sensor (Hall or inductive) reports the speed of the transmission output; it gives the gear ratio together with input speed and on many vehicles also the road speed for speedometer and cruise control. P0720 is the general circuit code. Ford also uses it for 'no signal': while engine and turbine speed show the vehicle moving, the sensor reports under 100–200 rpm for 5–30 s; ZF's 6HP26 in Ford vehicles flags an open or short after 0.6 s. Subaru-based systems (Saab 9-2X) flag an impossible 255 km/h or 0 km/h while driving and light the MIL after two trips, substituting the other sensor. GM does not use P0720 but P0722. Speedometer and cruise control may fail, often with a vehicle speed code as well.

causes.label: Speed sensor faulty (Hall IC or coil open or shorted)
Connector or harness corroded, chafed or loose pins (with internal sensors also the pass-through connector)
Metal debris on the sensor magnet or damaged reluctor wheel
Transmission module or its sensor supply faulty

symptoms: Speedometer drops out or jumps
Warning lamp, limp mode or fixed gear
Harsh shifts, cruise control not working

P0721.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0721.description: The output shaft speed sensor (Hall or inductive) reports the speed of the transmission output; it gives the gear ratio together with input speed and on many vehicles also the road speed for speedometer and cruise control. P0721 means the output speed is present but implausible: too high (Ford 6R80 above 7450 rpm), not matching wheel or input speed in the engaged gear (ZF 6HP26 more than 200 or 250 rpm apart, Ford's F21 more than 15 % for 10 s), or jumping (Allison 1000: 500 rpm within 0.15 s). On GM's 10-speed with a direction-sensing sensor, P0721 means the reported direction of rotation does not fit – since 2025 after two trips, earlier after one. Wrong tyre sizes or a faulty wheel speed sensor can also falsify the comparison.

causes.label: Output speed sensor faulty or dirty (metal debris)
Contact problems or interference in the sensor circuit
Wrong tyre size or axle ratio, faulty wheel speed sensor
Reluctor wheel damaged or sensor mounted wrongly

symptoms: Speedometer jumps
Warning lamp
Wrong shifts, limp mode
ABS/ESP warning possible if wheel speed is affected

P0722.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0722.description: The output shaft speed sensor (Hall or inductive) reports the speed of the transmission output; it gives the gear ratio together with input speed and on many vehicles also the road speed for speedometer and cruise control. P0722 means the output speed signal is missing while the vehicle is driving. GM's 2025 modules flag under 60 rpm for 3.5–5 s with more than 50 Nm torque and check wheel speeds as well; a 2006 GM table flags no output pulse during 6000 input pulses; Ford under 100–200 rpm for 5–30 s; Saab's Aisin box from 4 km/h. GM rates it after one trip. The transmission goes into limp mode, and speedometer and cruise control may stop working. On GM's 10-speed, P0717 and P0722 together point to the shared sensor supply.

causes.label: Speed sensor faulty (Hall IC or coil open or shorted)
Connector or harness corroded, chafed or loose pins (with internal sensors also the pass-through connector)
Metal debris on the sensor magnet or damaged reluctor wheel
Transmission module or its sensor supply faulty

symptoms: Speedometer reads 0
Limp mode or fixed gear
Warning lamp (MIL, transmission)
Cruise control not working

P0723.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0723.description: The output shaft speed sensor (Hall or inductive) reports the speed of the transmission output; it gives the gear ratio together with input speed and on many vehicles also the road speed for speedometer and cruise control. P0723 means the output speed drops or jumps briefly. GM's 2006 tables flag road speed falling below 61 rpm while driving; the 2019–2025 modules count sudden drops (for example 700 rpm) and fail after more than five, after one trip. In Ford vehicles the ZF 6HP26 flags a drop of more than 1000 rpm with the converter clutch locked, the CFT30 more than 6000 rpm per second. The speedometer needle twitches, shifts become erratic and limp mode may follow at times. Loose contacts are the usual cause.

causes.label: Loose contact, corroded connector or chafing
Electrical interference (shielding, ground, added consumers)
Metal debris on the sensor or loose mounting
Sensor faulty internally (temperature-dependent)

symptoms: Speedometer needle twitches or drops briefly
Occasional wrong shifts or downshift jolts
Warning lamp
Limp mode at times

P0724.title: Brake Switch B Circuit High
P0724.description: Brake switch B is the brake signal to the transmission module or a second brake switch channel, used to release the converter clutch, adapt shift strategy on grades and cancel cruise control. Low and high describe the signal voltage, and what that means depends on polarity: GM's converter clutch brake switch is closed at rest (12 V), while Saab's Trionic 8 sees 12 V when braking. Detection is always a plausibility check against driving: the brake reads applied during accelerations or never applied during decelerations. P0724 means the signal stays high. For GM that reads as brake never applied: 2006 transmission modules flag it after eight decelerations without a brake signal of at least 2 s, without MIL. Saab's Trionic 8 flags a brake light signal that reads on while accelerating from 3 to 40 km/h, four times, and disables cruise control. The opposite is P0719.

causes.label: Brake light switch sticking or misadjusted
Signal wire shorted to positive (Saab T8) or switch permanently closed (GM)
Retrofitted trailer or LED lights feeding back
Module input faulty

symptoms: Cruise control cannot be activated or switches off
Unusual shifting, converter clutch behaviour changed
No downshift on uphill grades (Subaru)
Brake lights stay off or on

P0725.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit
P0725.description: The transmission module needs engine speed for converter slip, shift quality and to check the turbine speed. Today it almost always arrives over CAN from the engine module with a validity flag; only GM's 2007 Allison 1000 tables show a separate engine speed sensor read by the transmission module. P0725 is the general fault of this input; with CAN it means the engine module marks its speed value as invalid. Saab's Aisin transmissions and a 2006 GM table set it after about 4 s, the GM table with immediate MIL. A Saab bulletin notes that behind P0725 there is always a crankshaft or camshaft sensor code in the engine module (P0016, P0335–P0339) – so read the engine module first. Limp mode follows; a completely missing CAN message is U0100.

causes.label: Crankshaft or camshaft sensor fault in the engine module (speed invalid there)
CAN fault between engine and transmission module (wiring, termination, connector)
Engine module software or fault
Transmission module faulty

symptoms: Transmission warning lamp, possibly check engine light
Torque converter clutch locked out
Harsh shifts or limp mode
Often an engine code (crankshaft sensor) as well

P0726.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Range/Performance
P0726.description: The transmission module needs engine speed for converter slip, shift quality and to check the turbine speed. Today it almost always arrives over CAN from the engine module with a validity flag; only GM's 2007 Allison 1000 tables show a separate engine speed sensor read by the transmission module. P0726 means the engine speed value is present but implausible. The Allison 1000, which reads its own sensor, flags a jump of 600 rpm within 0.15 s or noise of ±650 rpm, with the engine above 600 rpm and a gear engaged, after two trips. Saab's 9-3 of 2000, which receives the value over the bus, flags more than 7200 rpm for at least 10 s. The converter clutch is then locked out and shifts may be harsh. No signal at all is P0727.

causes.label: Engine speed sensor at the transmission (Allison) dirty or faulty, loose contact
Interference (shielding, ground)
Wrong bus value from the engine module (crankshaft sensor problem)
Transmission module

symptoms: Transmission warning lamp, possibly check engine light
Torque converter clutch locked out
Harsh shifts or limp mode
Often an engine code (crankshaft sensor) as well

P0727.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
P0727.description: The transmission module needs engine speed for converter slip, shift quality and to check the turbine speed. The module then works without converter slip information, usually locks out the converter clutch and may enter limp mode.

CAN communication between engine and transmission module disturbed
Crankshaft sensor fault in the engine module
Transmission module faulty

symptoms: Transmission warning lamp, possibly check engine light

Harsh shifts or limp mode

P0728.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent
P0728.description: The transmission module needs engine speed for converter slip, shift quality and to check the turbine speed. A loose contact in the signal or CAN circuit or an intermittent crankshaft sensor fault in the engine module is the likely cause; shifts may be harsh at times.

causes.label: Loose contact in signal or CAN circuit
Sensor (if fitted) dirty or loose
Intermittent crankshaft sensor fault in the engine module

symptoms: Occasional transmission warning lamp
Harsh shift now and then

P0729.title: Gear 6 Incorrect Ratio
P0729.description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0729 concerns sixth gear. Saab's Aisin six-speed also checks whether the actual ratio matches fourth or fifth – the sixth gear clutch is not holding and the box drops into another gear. Ford stores it only if the fault does not fit a particular solenoid (otherwise P0751 ff). On GM manual transmissions (LT4) it checks the gear position sensor instead.

causes.label: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated
Clutch for sixth gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in sixth gear, engine speed higher than expected
Harsh or delayed shifts
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P072A.title: Stuck in Neutral
P072A.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P072A means the transmission stays in neutral although a gear is commanded – no drive. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the DPS6 reports drum position faults under its own codes. On dual-clutch or automated manuals a drum or fork would fail to engage a gear, on planetary automatics clutch pressure would be missing. The opposite is P073D.

causes.label: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum A motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts
Limp mode, transmission warning
Clunking or blocking when shifting

P072B.title: Stuck in Reverse
P072B.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. P072B is the code for drum B: reverse cannot be disengaged. The transmission then locks out sub-gearbox B and can only use drum A (1st, 3rd, 5th), or the car is stranded. Slip in reverse is P0736.

Transmission module

P0730.title: Incorrect Gear Ratio
P0730.description: P0730 reports a wrong transmission ratio without assigning it to a gear. Two uses are documented. Older Aisin-type automatics (a 2006 GM table, Saab's 9-5 of 2002) set it when fourth or fifth gear shows the ratio of third – a shift solenoid (Saab: S3) is not switching; GM lights the MIL at once, Saab enters limp mode. GM's continuously variable transmissions of 2023 and 2025 use it when the pulleys do not reach the commanded variator ratio – the belt or chain slips or clamping pressure is too low – after one trip. Ford and newer GM step automatics use gear-specific or clutch valve codes instead. Check fluid level and condition first.

causes.label: Fluid level or quality (CVT fluid or ATF)
Shift solenoid or pressure control valve sticking or faulty
Clutch or brake wear, or worn variator belt, chain or pulleys
Faulty speed sensor signal

symptoms: Slipping, engine speed rises without drive
Wrong gear or missing upper gears, limp mode
Check engine light (GM) or transmission warning
CVT: judder, weak acceleration

P0731.title: Gear 1 Incorrect Ratio
P0731.description: The transmission module divides input (turbine) speed by output speed and compares the result with the ratio of the commanded gear; a deviation means slip – a clutch or brake not holding, too little pressure – or a wrong gear. Thresholds: Ford more than 30 rpm off for 1.8 s three times (diesel 2023: over 20 % for 12 s), GM's 2006 tables and the Allison 1000 converter slip of 200–230 rpm for 2.25 s after one trip, Saab's Aisin boxes over 20 % twelve times without MIL. P0731 concerns first gear. A 2006 GM table uses a tighter 4 % limit here and caps output speed at 1260 rpm; Saab's 2002 9-5 flags 3 % with the brake released. With a one-way clutch in first, slip shows as slipping when pulling away. On GM manual transmissions it checks the gear position sensor instead.

causes.label: Fluid level too low or fluid worn or contaminated
Clutch or brake for first gear worn (linings, piston seal)
Sticking shift or pressure valve, leaking valve body gasket, blocked passages
GM manual transmissions only: gear position sensor faulty or not learned

symptoms: Slipping or flare in first gear, engine speed higher than expected
Harsh or delayed shifts
Limp mode (Aisin: second gear and reverse only), transmission warning
Check engine light depending on manufacturer

P0737.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit
P0737.description: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0737 is the general circuit fault of this output; low and high are P0738/P0739. Not to be confused with the engine speed input at the transmission module (P0725 ff). A tachometer or dependent display then reads wrong or nothing, while driving is usually unaffected.

causes.label: Wire to the receiver open or shorted
Receiver (e.g. instrument cluster) shorted internally
Connector corroded
Driver stage in the transmission module faulty

symptoms: Tachometer or dependent display not working or wrong
Warning lamp depending on manufacturer
Usually no effect on driving

P0738.description: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. Warning lamp depending on manufacturer

P0739.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit High
P0739.description: Some transmission modules pass an engine speed signal on to other devices such as a tachometer over a wire of their own. CARB requires output circuits to be checked. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0737–P0739 – engine speed is shared over CAN today; the description follows CARB and the engine module's own speed output (P0654), which sends, for example, two pulses per revolution. P0739 means this output is too high, typically shorted to positive or, depending on the driver, open, so it can no longer switch to ground. The opposite is P0738, the general fault P0737. A tachometer or dependent display then reads nothing or full scale, while driving is usually unaffected.

causes.label: Output wire shorted to positive or open
Receiver faulty
Connector corroded
Driver stage in the transmission module faulty

symptoms: Tachometer shows nothing or full scale
Warning lamp depending on manufacturer
Usually no effect on driving

P073A.title: Stuck in Gear 5
P073A.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P073A is the code for drum A: fifth gear cannot be disengaged. The car stays in fifth – very weak pulling away – or sub-gearbox A is locked out. Slip in fifth gear is P0735.

causes.label: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum A motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts
Limp mode, transmission warning
Clunking or blocking when shifting

P073B.title: Stuck in Gear 6
P073B.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P073B is the code for drum B: sixth gear cannot be disengaged. The car stays in sixth – it can hardly pull away – or sub-gearbox B is locked out. Slip in sixth gear is P0729.

causes.label: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum B motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts
Limp mode, transmission warning
Clunking or blocking when shifting

P073C.title: Stuck in Gear 7
P073C.description: Ford's DPS6 dry dual-clutch transmission moves its gears with two electrically driven shift drums whose position is read by Hall sensors: drum A shifts 1st, 3rd and 5th, drum B reverse, 2nd, 4th and 6th. Ford's 2012 summary lists 'stuck in gear' codes for each drum: the module commands the drum out of a gear, but the gear stays engaged. It gives no thresholds or MIL rating. P073C would be the code for a seventh gear that cannot be disengaged, which only exists on transmissions with seven or more gears. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – the six-speed DPS6 has no seventh gear, GM's 9- and 10-speeds report clutch valve codes and Ford's 10R80 solenoid codes instead. causes.label: Shift fork or synchronizer for this gear sticking
Shift drum B motor, Hall position sensing or driver faulty
Transmission module
On planetary automatics: clutch or brake not releasing (sticking valve)

symptoms: Transmission stays in one gear, no further shifts
Limp mode, transmission warning
Clunking or blocking when shifting

P073D.title: Unable to Engage Neutral
P073D.description: P073D means neutral is commanded but not reached or not held. GM uses it on vehicles with electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire, e.g. Cadillac XT4): the selector or engine module compares commanded and actual range from the range sensor and flags it after 1.8–2 s in the selector module or 10 s in the engine module, after two trips. For Ford's 6F35 the supplier Sonnax describes a mechanical cause: a forward or direct clutch dragging in neutral, visible as turbine speed staying only 200–400 rpm below engine speed. The car may creep in N; range changes may be locked. The opposite, stuck in neutral, is P072A.

causes.label: Ford 6F35: forward or direct clutch dragging (balance piston, plates, seal)
Shift-by-wire: range actuator or park module, range sensor or its calibration
Valve body (manual valve, missing check ball, sticking solenoid)
CAN communication or control module

symptoms: Vehicle creeps in N or engine is loaded when shifting to N
N selection not accepted, warning message
Harsh engagement N to D/R (6F35)
Check engine light after two trips (GM)

P073E.title: Unable to Engage Reverse
P073E.description: P073E means reverse is commanded but not reached. Two uses are documented. With electronic gear selection (shift-by-wire) GM compares the commanded range with the actual range reported by the transmission and flags it if reverse is not reached within 1.8–3 s in the selector or diesel engine module, or 10 s in petrol engine modules, after two trips; GM bulletins name a range actuator centred wrongly (LaCrosse, XT5) and software after an over-the-air update (2025 Equinox/Terrain). On dual-clutch transmissions (2020–23 Corvette, Maserati MC20) it means the reverse gear cannot be engaged. Stuck in reverse is P072B, slip in reverse P0736.

causes.label: Range actuator or park module centred wrongly or faulty (shift-by-wire)
Module software (e.g. after an over-the-air update)
Range sensor reports the wrong actual range
Reverse clutch or brake, valve or shift fork (DCT)
Fluid level or system pressure

symptoms: No reverse, or R not accepted
Transmission warning, check engine light after two trips (GM)
Display shows R but the vehicle does not reverse

P073F.title: Unable to Engage Gear 1
P073F.description: 'Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P073F means the first gear, on the odd sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072C, slip in an engaged gear P0731. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.

causes.label: Shift fork valve or solenoid in the mechatronic unit sticking (dirt, wear)
System pressure unstable or too low (pressure valve, pump, fluid level)
Shift fork, sleeve, synchronizer or dogs damaged
Learned shift fork or clutch values lost or wrong
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Gear 1 skipped or not engaged
Transmission warning or check engine light, possibly limp mode with one sub-gearbox locked out
Jerking, delayed pulling away or shifting

P0740.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit/Open
P0740.description: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. P0740 concerns the control circuit of the converter clutch solenoid. Ford flags an open circuit when the driver feedback line disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with MIL; a 2006 GM table checks 0/12 V with more than 43 of 50 failed counts after two trips – newer GM units use P2761/P2763/P2764. FCA's Ram 6.7 reads P0740 as converter slip out of range and moved it to two trips by software in 2013. The clutch is then switched off: higher engine speed when cruising, more fuel, hotter fluid.

causes.label: Open or corroded harness or transmission pass-through connector
Converter clutch solenoid coil open
Internal transmission harness or mechatronic unit
Driver stage in the module faulty
FCA: actual converter slip (clutch wear, fluid) or software

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
No lock-up: engine speed about 100–300 rpm higher when cruising
Higher fuel consumption, hotter transmission fluid

P0741.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P0741.description: P0741 means the converter clutch does not lock although commanded – slip stays too high while the circuit is electrically fine. Thresholds: GM's T43 at least 130 rpm for 5 s twice, the 6T70 50 rpm for 5 s three times, Saab's Aisin AF40 over 100 rpm for 2 s, all after two trips; Ford over 100–200 rpm or a speed ratio below 0.93 over five lock-up events; Subaru engine speed more than 9/8 of target for 10.2 s. The module then locks out the clutch, sometimes the top gear, and uses a hot-mode shift pattern. Low or burnt fluid, a worn control valve in the valve body and a glazed converter clutch are the usual causes; Hyundai's 8-speed bulletin calls for a new converter.

causes.label: Fluid level too low, old or burnt fluid
Converter clutch control valve worn or sticking, bore worn
Lock-up clutch in the converter worn or glazed
Solenoid mechanically sluggish (electrically fine)
Leaking turbine shaft seals or pump

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
Higher engine speed when cruising, 'rubber band' feel
Higher consumption, rising fluid temperature
Possibly shudder when the clutch applies

P0742.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Stuck On
P0742.description: P0742 means the converter clutch stays applied although commanded off – there is almost no slip. GM's T43 flags −50 to +13 rpm for 1.5 s six times and the 6T70 −20 to +30 rpm for 2.5 s, both after one trip; Allison and Saab's Aisin AF40 after two trips, the AF40 also when the engine stalls without slip. Typical is the engine stalling when stopping or when selecting D or R, plus jerking at low speed. Note the different uses: Ford's P0742 is a short to ground in the clutch solenoid circuit (stuck on is P2758 there), and Saab's 9-3 of 2003 uses it for a mechanical lock-up fault.

causes.label: Converter clutch control valve sticking in the applied position
Solenoid stuck open (or short to ground with low-side control)
Lock-up clutch seized in the converter
Wrong fluid level or contaminated fluid
Engine or turbine speed signal implausible

symptoms: Engine stalls when stopping or selecting D/R
Jerking or bucking at low speed
Check engine light or transmission warning

P0743.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Electrical
P0743.description: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. P0743 is the collective electrical code for the converter clutch solenoid circuit – open, short to ground or to positive – detected by terminal voltage, driver feedback or current. Subaru flags it after 0.14 s and lights the MIL after two trips, Saab's 9-3 of 2003 above 1356 mA for 500 ms, Allison after 1.5 s; older Ford transmissions also use it. The clutch is switched off; Saab's Aisin boxes go into limp mode, Subaru does not.

causes.label: Transmission harness or pass-through connector (corrosion, chafing, oil in connector)
Solenoid coil open or shorted
Internal harness or mechatronic unit
Driver stage in the transmission or engine module

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
No lock-up: engine speed about 100–300 rpm higher when cruising
Limp mode on some makes (Saab/Aisin)

P0744.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Intermittent
P0744.description: The torque converter clutch (lock-up) connects pump and turbine mechanically; a solenoid – on/off, pulse-width modulated or proportional – moves a control valve in the valve body. Slip is engine speed minus turbine speed. Manufacturers do not use P0740–P0744 uniformly: Ford uses P0740 for open, P0742 for short to ground and P0744 for short to power, and reports stuck on as P2758. In J2012 P0744 is an intermittent fault in the converter clutch circuit, but no manufacturer document available to us uses it that way: Ford flags a short to power via the driver feedback line after 0.5–5 s with MIL, and Nissan's CVT bulletins treat it as a functional converter fault checked at the valve body and belt. GM does not use it. Short interruptions make the clutch drop out and reapply, and lock-up may be disabled for the trip.

causes.label: Loose contact or corrosion at the transmission connector or harness
Ford: control wire shorted to positive
Solenoid with temperature-dependent winding fault
Nissan CVT: converter or valve body mechanical

symptoms: Check engine light
Lock-up missing or jerky at times
Engine speed jumps when cruising

P0745.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A
P0745.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0745 is the general code for this valve; the sub-codes P0746–P0749 follow. It is documented on Mitsubishi CVTs as a current plausibility check: at most 400 mA while 750 mA or more is commanded for 5 s, or 1.34 A or more for 1 s. A failure usually leaves the valve unpowered, so pressure goes to maximum: harsh shifts and, depending on the transmission, limp mode in a fixed gear.

causes.label: Pressure control solenoid (coil) faulty
Transmission harness or connector
Contaminated fluid, valve sluggish
Transmission module

symptoms: Harsh shifts or engagement (maximum pressure)
Limp mode in a fixed gear
Transmission warning or check engine light

P0746.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0746.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0746 means the valve is electrically fine but the commanded pressure does not build. GM's clutch-to-clutch units detect it as slip: 400 rpm or more for 1.5 s (T87), or clutch 1 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s three times (9-speed), after one trip; Allison when the oncoming clutch does not apply. Mitsubishi's dual-clutch flags 500 mA current deviation. Slipping or flaring on shifts, a missed gear and limp mode follow; GM's 9-speed bulletin checks clutch plates and replaces the valve body.

causes.label: Pressure valve or spool worn or dirty
Fluid level too low, burnt fluid, clogged filter
Clutch plates or piston seals of the affected clutch worn
Line pressure too low (pump, main regulator)
Learned values missing after repair

symptoms: Slipping or engine flare on shifts
Gear not reached, limp mode in a fixed gear
Check engine light or transmission warning

P0747.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Stuck On
P0747.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. 'A' is usually the line pressure valve, on GM clutch-to-clutch transmissions (6T, 8L, 9T) the pressure valve of clutch 1. Ford does not use P0745–P0749 but P0960–P0963. P0747 means the valve is electrically fine but pressure stays applied. On GM's clutch-to-clutch units the off-going clutch 1 does not release – slip stays below 50 rpm (9-speed, 0.8 s on loaded downshifts), and Allison flags 25 rpm or less for 0.3–1 s, both after one trip. On line pressure valves it means permanently high pressure. Harsh, abrupt shifts, a tied-up transmission and a default gear follow. GM noted false settings on 2017 8-speeds: clear and retest first.

causes.label: Pressure or clutch valve or spool sticking (dirt, debris)
Valve body worn
Software or false setting
Wrong or contaminated fluid
Clutch plates stuck or burnt

symptoms: Harsh, abrupt shifts
Transmission ties up, engine speed drops on shifts
Limp mode or default gear
Check engine light

P0748.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Electrical
P0748.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. P0748 is the electrical code of this valve, checked by current, duty cycle or terminal voltage: Subaru after 0.14 s with MIL after two trips and limp mode in third, Allison against an 8 Ω current model after 125 ms, GM's diesel 4L80-E for a duty cycle outside 0.5–95 % for 2 s without MIL. Saab's 2010 9-5 uses P0748 for a current deviation instead.

Pressure control solenoid faulty (resistance out of spec)
Internal harness, electronic module or mechatronic unit
System voltage too low
Transmission module driver

symptoms: Harsh shifts or engagement (maximum pressure)
Limp mode in a fixed gear
Transmission warning or check engine light
Reduced engine power (torque limit)

P0749.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Intermittent
P0749.description: Pressure control solenoid A sets line or clutch pressure by current; most are 'normally high', so with no current – as in limp mode – maximum pressure applies. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; Mitsubishi defines the sister code for valve B (P0779) as circuit open or shorted to positive for 1 s. Chafed harness (intermittent short)
Valve with temperature-dependent winding fault
Voltage dips or poor ground

symptoms: Harsh shifts at times
Occasional limp mode, normal again after restart
Warning lamp (sometimes only stored)

P074A.title: Unable to Engage Gear 2
P074A.description: 'Unable to engage' means the transmission does not reach the commanded gear – the opposite of 'stuck in gear', where a gear cannot be disengaged. Documented users are dual-clutch transmissions, whose shift forks are moved hydraulically and watched by travel sensors: GM's 8-speed in the 2020–23 Corvette, Maserati's MC20 and – for the odd gears only – Acura's RLX Sport Hybrid, whose 'odd gear monitor' is part of an emission recall with permanent codes. No manufacturer publishes thresholds. P074A means the second gear, on the even sub-gearbox, cannot be engaged; a gear that will not disengage is P072D, slip in an engaged gear P0732. GM's bulletin first runs a learn procedure and cleans valves only if system pressure codes are present; Maserati checks system pressure (20–30 bar). If neither helps, the mechanics are at fault.

System pressure unstable or too low (pressure valve, pump, fluid level)
Shift fork, sleeve, synchronizer or dogs damaged
Learned shift fork or clutch values lost or wrong
Module software or calibration

symptoms: Gear 2 skipped or not engaged
Transmission warning or check engine light, possibly limp mode with one sub-gearbox locked out
Jerking, delayed pulling away or shifting

P0750.title: Shift Solenoid A
P0750.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. Manufacturers use these codes differently: Ford reports an open circuit with the base code and shorts separately, newer GM units have separate low/high codes, and the letter is not tied to a valve number (Saab's 9-5: A = valve S2). P0750 is the general code for solenoid A and is used in practice for an open circuit: Ford's step automatics (2012–2023) set it when the smart driver feedback disagrees with the command for 0.5–5 s, with shorts to ground and power as P0973/P0974; Ram's 6.7 L with Aisin transmission calls it 'control circuit open', and a 2023 bulletin traces it to a leaking capacitor in the engine module. GM does not use P0750. With the solenoid unpowered the transmission falls back to a hydraulic default gear with maximum pressure.

causes.label: Open or corroded wire or transmission pass-through connector
Solenoid coil open or shorted
Internal harness or electronic module in the transmission
Module driver faulty or valve supply missing

symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Limp mode in a fixed gear, no upshifts
Harsh shifts from maximum line pressure

P0751.title: Shift Solenoid A Performance/Stuck Off
P0751.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; together the solenoid states select the gear, and the module checks the result by gear ratio, slip or a pressure switch – the pattern of wrong gears shows which solenoid hangs off or on. P0751 means solenoid A is commanded on but valve, clutch or gear do not follow. GM's 6T70 flags a ratio of 1.34–1.48 with slip of 400 rpm for 0.3 s eight times and locks out first gear; GM 4-speeds recognise the pattern 2-2-3-3; both after two trips. Allison checks its pressure switch for 5 s after one trip. Ford's 'functionally failed off' covers the whole clutch circuit, and its 10R80 and 8F35 bulletins show purely mechanical causes such as a leaking clutch cylinder.

causes.label: Shift spool in the valve body sticking (dirt, debris)
Internal leak or clutch fault in the circuit
Solenoid mechanically sluggish or screen clogged
Fluid level or quality wrong

symptoms: Gears missing or skipped
Pulling away in the wrong gear, weak acceleration
Limp mode or gear lock-out
Check engine light

P0752.title: Shift Solenoid A Stuck On
P0752.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body; together the solenoid states select the gear, and the module checks the result by gear ratio, slip or a pressure switch – the pattern of wrong gears shows which solenoid hangs off or on. P0752 means solenoid A is commanded off but its clutch stays applied. GM's 6T70 flags slip of 400 rpm for 2 s five times after one trip and then runs only reverse, first and third with maximum pressure; GM's T43 a ratio of 3.83–4.23 (first instead of fourth); GM 4-speeds the pattern 1-1-4-4 after two trips; Allison its pressure switch after 2 s. Ford calls it 'functionally failed on'. A clutch that does not release can tie up the transmission.

causes.label: Shift spool sticking in the applied position
Solenoid stuck open or leaking
Clutch not releasing (burnt or stuck)
Contaminated or wrong fluid

symptoms: Wrong, often too low gear, engine revs high
Tie-up or jolt on shifts
Limp mode (GM: reverse, 1st, 3rd only)
Check engine light

P0753.title: Shift Solenoid A Electrical
P0753.description: A shift solenoid is an electrically switched valve in the valve body. P075F.title: Transmission Fluid Level Too High

P0771.title: Shift Solenoid E Performance/Stuck Off
P0771.description: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0771 is Ford's functional check by gear ratio over 10 events (2012) or 3 (2020–23, 2023 diesel). On the 6R80/6F it means the multiplex valve stays in its rest position, so solenoid D acts on the wrong clutch; valve and spool cannot be told apart. On the 6R140 the 4-5-6 clutch does not apply. Ford counts the whole clutch system in, and its 10R80 and 8F35 bulletins list P0771 with mechanical repairs. Slipping or missing gears and limp mode follow.

causes.label: Valve body or multiplex valve sticking (debris, dirt)
Clutch, piston seal or clutch cylinder leaking or worn
Fluid level low or fluid contaminated
Solenoid E mechanically stuck

symptoms: Slipping or flare on shifts
Missing gear (e.g. 4th–6th)
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0772.title: Shift Solenoid E Stuck On
P0772.description: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F35/6F55 it is an on/off valve that moves a multiplex valve, so solenoid D feeds either the low/reverse brake or the 4-5-6 clutch; on the 6R140 and 5R110W it is a proportional clutch valve with separate short codes (P0985/P0986). On Saab's Aisin 5-speed E is valve S1. P0772 is the counterpart of P0771: the gear ratio shows that the multiplex valve is stuck in its spring-loaded position (6R80/6F) or that the clutch controlled by solenoid E does not release (6R140: 4-5-6 clutch). Ford flags it after 10 or 3 events, continuously, and again counts valve, spool and clutch in; its 10R80 bulletins list it for harsh or delayed shifts. Harsh shifts, tie-up and a wrong gear follow.

causes.label: Multiplex or shift spool sticking
Clutch plates stuck or burnt, piston hanging
Solenoid E stuck open
Contaminated fluid

symptoms: Harsh shift jolt, transmission ties up
Limp mode in a fixed gear
Check engine light

P0774.description: What shift solenoid E does depends on the transmission. P0775.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B
P0775.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0775 is the general code for valve B. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; the trade journal MOTOR names it as a performance code of line pressure valve B on Ford's 5R55, set together with ratio codes after a broken overdrive servo. Sub-codes for performance, stuck on, electrical and intermittent follow (P0776–P0779).

causes.label: Valve body or pressure valve B worn or dirty
Line pressure wrong (load signal, main regulator)
Fluid condition
Circuit or coil

symptoms: Harsh or slipping shifts
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0776.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance/Stuck Off
P0776.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0776 means the valve is electrically fine but pressure stays too low. GM's 8-speed flags gear slip of 400 rpm for 1.5 s three times, the 9-speed clutch 2 slip over 200 rpm for 3 s, the CVT primary pressure below 200 kPa for 3 s – all after one trip. Mitsubishi's Jatco CVT flags secondary pressure 1.2 MPa off target; Nissan's bulletin calls for a mechanical CVT repair, a GM 6T70 bulletin a broken wave spring. Slipping, missing gears or lack of drive and limp mode follow.

causes.label: Clutch, return spring or piston seal of the assigned clutch faulty
Valve body or pressure valve dirty or worn
CVT belt or pulley damaged (CVT)
Fluid level low, fluid worn, filter clogged

symptoms: Slipping or missing gears
CVT: hesitation, lack of power
Limp mode
Check engine light

P0777.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On
P0777.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2.
