GM's 9-speed flags clutch 2 slip below 50 rpm for 0.8 s on loaded downshifts, the 8-speed uses a torque and inertia phase test, Allison 25 rpm or less – all after one trip. GM's Honda-built five-speed cannot always separate it from P0746 and stores both. Harsh shift jolts, tie-up and a default gear follow.

Clutch stuck or piston hanging
Contaminated fluid (debris after clutch damage)
Software or false setting

symptoms: Harsh shift jolt, transmission ties up
Limp mode in a fixed gear

P0778.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Electrical
P0778.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. causes.label: Harness or connector shorted or open
Pressure valve B coil faulty – often only replaceable with the valve body
Transmission module faulty
System voltage

symptoms: Harsh engagement jolt
Weak pulling away and acceleration
Limp mode (Saab: second and reverse only)
Check engine light

P0779.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Intermittent
P0779.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. In J2012 P0779 is an intermittent fault of valve B. The only manufacturer use found differs: Mitsubishi's 2022 Jatco CVT sets P0779 for an open circuit or short to positive in the secondary pressure valve circuit after 1 s (short to ground is P0778). The transmission then engages harshly, accelerates weakly and does not lock up.

causes.label: Connector or wire open or loose contact
Short to positive in the harness
Valve coil faulty

symptoms: Harsh engagement at times
Weak acceleration, no lock-up
Check engine light

P077A.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Loss of Direction Signal
P077A.description: Some transmissions use an output shaft speed sensor that also reports direction of rotation: in a GM patent two offset Hall elements send one pulse per tooth whose width encodes forward or reverse. The direction is needed to detect rolling back on a hill (a Hyundai patent raises idle speed then), for hill hold, stop-start and the forward/reverse change. P077A means the sensor still delivers speed pulses but no usable direction information – the pulse width stays outside the direction windows or one Hall element has failed. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; GM checks direction coherence under P0721. Hill hold, auto hold or stop-start may then be disabled and the forward/reverse change runs in a substitute mode.

causes.label: Output speed sensor faulty (one Hall element or direction channel failed)
Contact resistance in connector or wiring distorts the pulse
Wrong replacement sensor without direction function
Reluctor wheel damaged or air gap too large

symptoms: Transmission warning or check engine light depending on manufacturer
Hill hold, auto hold or stop-start unavailable
Rolling back on a hill not caught

P077B.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Direction Error
P077B.description: Some transmissions use an output shaft speed sensor that also reports direction of rotation: in a GM patent two offset Hall elements send one pulse per tooth whose width encodes forward or reverse. The direction is needed to detect rolling back on a hill (a Hyundai patent raises idle speed then), for hill hold, stop-start and the forward/reverse change. P077B means the sensor reports a direction that does not fit – for example reverse while a forward gear is engaged and the input and intermediate shaft sensors confirm forward motion. GM's transmission modules list P077B as a blocking condition for other checks, but run the actual check under their own codes: direction contradicts the gear for 2.5 s above 500 rpm, after one trip. Speed and direction are then unreliable: hill hold and the park and reverse logic fall back to substitute modes.

causes.label: Output speed sensor faulty (direction evaluation disturbed)
Wrong or incorrectly fitted sensor (orientation to the wheel)
Reluctor wheel damaged, metal debris on the sensor
Faulty reference (input or intermediate shaft sensor)

symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
Hill hold off
Limp mode possible
Speedometer or cruise control unreliable

P077C.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Low
P077C.description: GM's transmission modules from 2019 to 2025 (9- and 10-speeds) also read the active output speed sensor's line voltage as an analog value. P077C means this voltage is below 0.25 V – a short to ground of under about 0.5 Ω between signal and module ground – for more than 0.05 s with the system above 10 V; GM rates it after one trip. GM then blocks the no-signal and ratio checks so that P0722 is not set instead of the actual short. Without output speed the transmission enters limp mode and road speed may be missing. On GM's 10-speed input and output sensors share a supply.

causes.label: Signal or supply wire shorted to ground (chafing at the case)
Sensor shorted internally
Oil or moisture in the connector, corrosion
Module input faulty

symptoms: Check engine light at once (GM)
Limp mode or fixed gear
Speedometer or cruise control failed
Harsh shifts, no converter lock-up

P077D.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit High
P077D.description: GM's transmission modules from 2019 to 2025 (9- and 10-speeds) also read the active output speed sensor's line voltage as an analog value. P077D is the mirror of P077C: the voltage is above 4.75 V – a short to the module supply of under about 0.5 Ω – for more than 0.05 s, after one trip. GM then blocks the no-signal and ratio checks; a GM hybrid also blocks its idle diagnosis. Without usable output speed the transmission enters limp mode, and speedometer or cruise control may fail.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to sensor supply or battery voltage
Sensor faulty internally
Ground fault at the sensor, corroded connector
Module input

symptoms: Check engine light at once (GM)
Limp mode
Speedometer or cruise control failed
Shift problems

P077E.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Measurement System Multiple Sensor Correlation
P077E.description: P077E is a plausibility check between several fluid temperature readings – for example sensors A and B, sump and valve body, or the module's internal temperature. If they differ by more than allowed after a settling time, such as a long stop, the code sets, without being able to blame a single sensor. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM checks each sensor alone (P0711, with the module temperature on the 6T70), and Ford has no multi-sensor check. A substitute value then limits converter clutch and shift adaption.

causes.label: One temperature sensor drifting (aged NTC)
Contact resistance at a sensor connector or wire
Fluid level too low (sensor not wetted)
Module or software

symptoms: Transmission warning, possibly check engine light
Converter clutch applies late or not at all
Harsh cold shifts

P077F.title: Reverse 2 Incorrect Ratio
P077F.description: P077F checks the ratio in a second reverse gear: input speed divided by output speed lies outside the tolerance band around the target ratio – a slipping clutch, a wrong gear or a sensor fault. Only transmissions with two reverse ratios need it, such as Mercedes' 7G-Tronic (−3.42 and −2.23, with the second reverse kept in limp mode) and its 5G-Tronic predecessor; GM's 9- and 10-speeds, Ford's 10R and ZF's 8HP have one. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code; the check works like the other ratio codes such as P0736.

causes.label: Slipping clutch or brake in the second reverse power path
Fluid level low or fluid worn
Solenoid or pressure regulator sticking
Faulty input or output speed sensor

symptoms: Reverse slips or engages late
Limp mode
Transmission warning or check engine light

P0780.title: Shift Error
P0780.description: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. Ford does not use P0780–P0784 (its shift completion check feeds the solenoid codes), nor do GM's 2018–2025 tables. P0780 is the collective code when the faulty shift is not assigned to a gear. GM's 2006 Aisin-type five-speed counts five shifts that are too long, too short or tied up with fluid above 60 °C and lights the MIL at once; GM's Honda-built unit flags a 3–4 shift that stays in the lower ratio after two trips; Saab's 2010 Aisin six-speed counts ten faulty shifts without MIL, limits torque and keeps second and reverse. Nissan fixed P0780 on the 2021 Rogue CVT with new software.

causes.label: Fluid level wrong, fluid worn or contaminated
Valve body, shift or pressure valve sticking
Worn clutches or bands (mechanical damage)
Module software or shift adaption
Faulty speed sensor signal

symptoms: Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Engine flare during shifts
Warning lamp
Limp mode with fixed gear, reduced power

P0781.title: 1-2 Shift
P0781.description: Shift codes are a functional check of the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded shift with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, is too short or abrupt, does not happen, flares or ties up. P0781 names the 1–2 shift as the faulty one, up or down; slip in a steady gear is reported by the ratio codes instead. Lexus' AB60F six-speed (LX 570, 2008–11) lists P0781 among its transmission performance codes; the bulletin first checks fluid level, then installs new software and, if needed, a new transmission. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P0781.

P0785.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A
P0785.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P0785 is the general circuit code for solenoid A. GM's 2006 tables use it for the 3-2 downshift solenoid circuit (more than 43 of 50 failed counts, after one trip); Saab's 2002 Aisin box for an open or short in the SLS circuit with warning lamp and limp mode; Hyundai's Genesis bulletins for the drive solenoid, replacing valve and electronic module and then the module if it returns. Limp mode, harsh 3-2 downshifts or – on the Genesis – no drive follow.

causes.label: Solenoid coil open or shorted
Connector or wire at the transmission (oil, corrosion)
Electronic module or transmission module driver

symptoms: Warning lamp
Limp mode
Harsh 3-2 downshift (GM) or rough shifts (Aisin)
Genesis shift-by-wire: drive cannot be engaged

P0786.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Range/Performance
P0786.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). Unstable system voltage

Warning lamp

P0787.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Low
P0787.description: 'Shift timing solenoid' means different parts: on GM's 4L60-E the 3-2 downshift solenoid that times the band apply on that downshift, on Aisin five-speeds (GM, Saab) the linear valve SLS that sets clutch pressure during the shift, and on the 2017–18 Genesis G80/G90 with shift-by-wire the on/off solenoids that engage drive (A) and reverse (B). P078F.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit
P078F.description: P078F is the circuit fault of a third transmission mode switch (C), after A (P071A–P071C) and B (P071D–P071F): its state is invalid or implausible. GM's transmission modules of 2023 and 2025 list the number only as a blocking condition for another check, without a description of their own; GM reports its drive mode selector today under P05D0–P05D3 (8-step resistor ladder, two trips). No manufacturer document available to us describes P078F itself. The mode then cannot be selected and the transmission stays on its normal schedule.

causes.label: Switch or button faulty or sticking
Wire or connector open or shorted
Moisture or dirt in the centre console
Control module

symptoms: Drive mode (sport, winter, tow) cannot be selected
Mode indicator missing
Transmission stays on the normal program

P0790.title: Normal/Performance Switch Circuit
P0790.description: P0790 is the circuit fault of the normal/performance (sport or power program) selector of an automatic transmission – the older single code that preceded the mode switch codes P071A ff; the early J2012 list still called it 'circuit malfunction'. The switch is usually a button to ground or a resistor ladder; a fault is an invalid level, a permanently pressed button or an open circuit. No manufacturer document available to us describes it; GM uses P05D0–P05D3 for its drive mode selector today. The sport program is then unavailable or permanently on.

causes.label: Button faulty or sticking
Wire or connector open or shorted
Liquid in the console
Control module

symptoms: Sport or performance program unavailable or always on
Mode indicator missing or flashing

P0791.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0791.description: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. Together with turbine and output speed it lets the module check each gear stage and control clutch slip. Ford uses P0791 as its only intermediate shaft code, for 'no or too little signal': while the vehicle drives under power (turbine at least 1500 rpm, output at least 650 rpm or 15 mph), the sensor reports below 250 rpm for 5 s – in the 2012 and 2020–23 summaries, with MIL. A Toyota bulletin for the U760 (Highlander, Venza, Camry 2009–10) replaces the countershaft sensor for P0791/P0793. GM's 10-speed has two such sensors but uses its own codes. Limp mode and harsh shifts follow.

causes.label: Intermediate shaft speed sensor faulty
Connector or wire at the transmission (oil, corrosion, chafing)
Reluctor wheel damaged or debris on the sensor
Control module

symptoms: Check engine light
Limp mode or fixed gear
Harsh or delayed shifts
Follow-up pressure control codes (Toyota)

P0792.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0792.description: The intermediate shaft speed sensor measures a shaft between input and output – a countershaft on Toyota's U760 six-speed, the intermediate shaft behind the overdrive set on Ford's 5R110W. P0792 means a signal is present but implausible: intermediate shaft speed does not match turbine or output speed for the detected gear stage, exceeds a maximum or jumps unrealistically. No manufacturer document available to us uses this code – Ford uses only P0791, Toyota's bulletin P0791/P0793, GM its own codes; the logic follows GM's range checks for input and output sensors (P0716/P0721). symptoms: Check engine light or transmission warning
Shift problems

P0795.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C
P0795.description: Pressure control solenoids are current-controlled proportional valves, and what B and C mean depends on the design: on GM's clutch-to-clutch automatics they are the pressure valves of clutches 2 and 3, on GM's CVT B is primary pulley pressure and C line pressure, on Jatco CVTs B is the secondary pressure valve, on Saab's AF40 B and C are clutch valves SLC1/SLC2. P0795 is the general code for valve C. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM's 8-speed uses only P0796/P0797 for its clutch 3 valve, Saab's AF40 only P0798 for valve SLC2. Sub-codes for performance, stuck on, electrical and intermittent follow (P0796–P0799).

symptoms: Shift problems

P079A.title: Transmission Friction Element A Slip Detected
P079A.description: The 'friction element slip' codes monitor a clutch that is commanded locked in a power-split hybrid transmission: the module calculates its slip from electric motor, engine and output speeds (target 0 rpm) and flags slip above a threshold for a minimum time, with sufficient line pressure and clutch torque; from 2016 GM also flags a calculated friction energy threshold at once. The letter matches the manufacturer's clutch number. P079A concerns clutch 1. On GM's Two-Mode SUVs and pickups (2008–13) that is the hybrid low/1-2 clutch, flagged above 200 rpm for 3 s after one trip; GM bulletins link it to a clogged line pressure orifice and the auxiliary oil pump. Too little line pressure: low or aged fluid, filter, auxiliary oil pump or blocked pressure orifice
Pressure or shift valve of clutch A or valve body sticking
Module software (false setting)
Faulty speed signals (motor resolver, output)

symptoms: Check engine light or 'service hybrid system' message
Limp mode with reduced power or restricted drive mode
Slipping, engine speed rises without drive
Jolt when the engine starts or stops

P07A2.title: Transmission Friction Element A Performance/Stuck Off
P07A2.description: Each friction element (clutch or brake) has three functional codes: slip while commanded locked (P079A ff), performance/stuck off – it does not apply or applies too weakly – and stuck on – it does not release. Ford's DPS6 PowerShift dry dual-clutch (Fiesta, Focus) uses it for clutch A – input shaft 1 with gears 1, 3 and 5 – as 'functionally stuck off', next to the electrical codes of its electric clutch actuator; Ford publishes no thresholds. P07CB.title: Transmission Fluid Thermostat Performance
P07CB.description: Many automatics have a thermostat in the fluid cooler circuit or a coolant-to-oil heat exchanger: a BMW patent describes a wax thermostat that bypasses the cooler until about 76 °C, a Ford patent a heat exchanger that warms transmission fluid from the coolant after a cold start. P07CB means this thermostat does not work as expected: fluid warms up too slowly (stuck open) or overheats (stuck closed). P07D7.title: Stuck in Gear 8

P07E4.title: Unable to Engage Park
P07E4.description: With shift-by-wire or park-by-wire, P, R, N and D are requested electrically (buttons, rotary selector, automatic park on shutdown) and an actuator moves the selector shaft or the park pawl; the module compares the requested with the range actually reached. P07E4 means park is not reached or not held within the allowed time. GM gives thresholds: 2 s in 2018 tables and the ICCM of its electronic range selector (2000 ms), 6–10 s in later tables, type B with the MIL after two trips; a 2018 bulletin for LaCrosse and XT5 blames a misaligned coupling of the range control module. Ford sets it with the wrench lamp instead of the MIL – on the 2020 Escape and Corsair a misrouted park release cable, on the Mach-E software – and applies the electric parking brake. Ram 1500 (2019) sets the MIL; Stellantis names a used manual park release as the most common cause.

Control module software

P07E5.title: Unable to Engage Drive

Only GM documents it: its electronic range selector (LaCrosse, XT5, XT4, 2025 Equinox and Terrain) allows 10 s in most tables, 3 s in the 2018 Diesel table and 2000 ms in the selector module, type B with the MIL after two trips. A 2018 bulletin blames a misaligned range control module coupling, its 2019 revision adds ratio codes; on the 2025 Equinox and Terrain it can appear after an over-the-air update and clears after a ten-minute rest. P07E7.title: Stuck in Drive

symptoms: Range stays in D despite the selector request
P or N cannot be reached, warning message
Warning lamp (depends on manufacturer)

P07E8.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit/Open
P07E8.description: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07E8 is the open-circuit check of these sensor lines: if one sensor input is pulled above 4.5 V for 2.4 s with the ignition on, the code sets. Mitsubishi lists it with the MIL but without a fail-safe reaction, because the remaining sensors still identify the position. Low and high are P07EA/P07EB. GM and Ford use their own codes for their selectors.

causes.label: Wire or connector between selector and shift module open
Position sensor in the selector faulty
Shift module input faulty

symptoms: Electric shift or check engine warning
Usually no noticeable restriction
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07E9.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Performance
P07E9.description: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07E9 is the plausibility check of the sensor voltage: valid levels lie only in defined on and off windows, and a sensor sitting for 2.4 s in a forbidden band in between (0.6–1.07, 2.12–2.67 or 3.28–4.5 V) sets it – typically contact resistance, moisture or a sensor beginning to fail. Mitsubishi defines no fail-safe reaction. Note the title: 'Circuit Performance', not 'Range/Performance'.

causes.label: Corroded or damp connector, contact resistance
Position sensor drifting
Shift module input

symptoms: Electric shift or check engine warning
Usually no noticeable restriction
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07EA.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Low
P07EA.description: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07EA is the electrical low check: one sensor reads below 0.6 V for 2.4 s – a signal wire shorted to ground or a missing sensor supply. Mitsubishi defines no fail-safe reaction. If all bits drop out at once, P07EF follows and the transmission goes to neutral.

Sensor supply in the selector open
Selector or module faulty

symptoms: Electric shift or check engine warning
Usually no noticeable restriction
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07EB.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit High
P07EB.description: Despite its name, 'Transmission Range Control A' is not the range actuator motor – that has its own codes, P272A and P272B – but the sensor circuits of an electric shift-by-wire selector. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 service manual for a CVT with electric shift (very likely the 2022–23 Outlander): the lever carries eight position sensors whose on/off pattern encodes R, N, home, D and M. P07EB is the electrical high check: one sensor reads above 4.5 V for 2.4 s, a signal wire shorted to the supply. Mitsubishi uses the same threshold as for the open circuit P07E8 and separates the two only in its list of causes; there is no fail-safe reaction.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to 5 V or 12 V supply
Selector faulty internally
Shift module

symptoms: Electric shift or check engine warning
Usually no noticeable restriction
Further sensor faults lead to P07EC/P07ED

P07EC.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit
P07EC.description: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EC sets when a single bit does not change as the lever moves through its positions – it is stuck on or off. The other bits still identify the position, but the decision takes at least a second. Mitsubishi shows only the yellow electric-shift warning, without the MIL. Two or more stuck bits are P07ED.

causes.label: One position sensor in the selector faulty
One sensor wire open or shorted
Dirt or sticking mechanism in the selector

symptoms: Yellow shift warning or message
Selected range taken over with a delay of a second or more
No MIL (Mitsubishi)

P07ED.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Stuck
P07ED.description: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07ED is the step after P07EC: at least two bits are stuck, so the position can no longer be decoded reliably. Mitsubishi then puts the drive in neutral and blocks changes between P, R, N and D, lights the MIL and the red or yellow shift warning; the car cannot be driven and has to be towed.

causes.label: Selector sensor board faulty
Selector connector corroded or loose (several pins)
Liquid spilled into the center console

symptoms: No range can be selected, vehicle in neutral
MIL and red or yellow shift warning
Vehicle cannot be driven (tow)

P07EE.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Range/Performance
P07EE.description: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EE is the range and plausibility fault of the position code; Mitsubishi assigns it solely to the electric shift module itself – the pattern fits no position or contradicts itself. A generic scan tool shows the fault as P0914 'Gear Shift Position Circuit A'. Shifting is blocked, the drive goes to neutral and the MIL comes on; the usual repair is a software update or the module.

causes.label: Electric shift module faulty (hardware or software)
Outdated module software
Selector or harness

symptoms: Vehicle goes to neutral, shifting blocked
MIL and shift warning
Generic scan tool shows P0914

P07EF.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Low
P07EF.description: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07EF is the low state of the whole pattern: all eight bits report off, which is no valid code – typically a disconnected selector plug or a missing common supply or ground. Mitsubishi detects it already at standstill after about 10 s with the ignition on, puts the drive in neutral and lights the MIL.

causes.label: Selector plug disconnected or its supply or ground open
Selector sensor board faulty
Electric shift module

symptoms: Vehicle in neutral, no range selectable
MIL and shift warning
Fault appears right after switching the ignition on

P07F0.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit High
P07F0.description: 'Transmission Range Multi-Function Select' is the multi-bit code of the shift-by-wire selector position: each position produces a fixed pattern of sensor states, and the module checks the pattern for logic errors. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift uses eight sensors (R: 1–2 on, N toward R: 1–5, home: all, N toward D: 4–8, D/M: 7–8). P07F0 would be the high counterpart of P07EF: the position code reports a high state that matches no valid position, for example signal levels pulled up by a short to the supply. No manufacturer document available to us uses it – on Mitsubishi's selector 'all on' is the valid home position, so a high state cannot be told apart there. By analogy to P07EF a module would block range changes or select neutral.

causes.label: Selector signal wires shorted to the supply
Selector faulty
Shift module

symptoms: Shift warning or MIL (depends on manufacturer)
Range selection blocked or neutral

P07F1.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit
P07F1.description: P07F1 is the general circuit code of a third input or turbine shaft speed sensor, after sensor A (P0715) and B (P2765); low and high for sensor C are P07C3 and P07C4. No production use could be found in GM tables from 2015 to 2025, Ford's summaries of 2012 and 2020–23, Mitsubishi's code index or manufacturer bulletins; such a sensor would make sense on transmissions with three input shafts or a hybrid input. The check would follow P0715: no plausible signal while driving or an open circuit. The module then uses a substitute value, keeps the converter clutch open and shifts more harshly; with emissions impact CARB requires the MIL.

causes.label: Sensor wire or connector open
Speed sensor faulty
Control module or software

symptoms: Check engine lamp (expected)
Harsh shifts, converter clutch stays open
Limp mode possible

P07F2.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit
P07F2.description: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F2 reports a fault in its communication. Mitsubishi's 2022 CVT with electric shift sets it when the module's start-up CAN check fails and blames the module itself; it switches to neutral only if the CVT or the whole system is affected too, and one of its two entries carries no MIL. GM (U18AA, U2409) and Ford (U101F, without MIL) report the same function under their own U codes.

causes.label: Shift-by-wire module faulty or its software
Communication wire or connector
Weak battery during start-up

symptoms: Shift warning
Usually no restriction; neutral if the transmission is affected too
U codes in other modules possible

P07F3.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit Low
P07F3.description: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F3 is the electrical low check of its communication line: the line is shorted to ground and stays at a low level. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; the code fits a dedicated signal or redundancy line between selector, range control module and transmission or engine module rather than a CAN bus. GM handles a bus short under its own U2409 (bus off for 1 s, two trips). The module may block range changes or select neutral.

causes.label: Communication wire shorted to ground
Module output stage faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

symptoms: Shift warning
Possible shift lock or neutral (depends on manufacturer)

P07F4.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit High
P07F4.description: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F4 is the electrical high check of its communication line: the line is shorted to the supply and stays at a high level. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; as with P07F3 it fits a dedicated signal or redundancy line rather than a CAN bus, whose faults GM reports under its own U codes. The module may block range changes or select neutral.

causes.label: Communication wire shorted to the supply
Module faulty
Connector fault

symptoms: Shift warning
Possible shift lock or neutral (depends on manufacturer)

P07F5.title: Transmission Range Control Module System Voltage Low
P07F5.description: The transmission range control module is the separate shift-by-wire control unit that reads the selector and drives the range actuator. P07F5 means its supply voltage is too low. No manufacturer document available to us uses the generic code, but GM checks exactly this under its own P17B0: battery voltage at the range control module at or below 9 V for 5 s within a 6 s window, type C without MIL. With too little voltage the actuator may not set the range or park pawl reliably; GM also suspends further checks of the module. A weak battery or a resistance in the module's fuse, supply or ground is the usual cause.

causes.label: Weak battery or charging system
Fuse, supply or ground wire of the module with high resistance
High actuator motor current on a weak supply

symptoms: Shift warning
Range or park lock reacts late or not at all
Often together with battery voltage codes

P07F6.title: Gear 9 Incorrect Ratio
P07F6.description: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07F6 covers 9th gear. Ford's 10R80 bulletins from 2023 to 2025 (F-150, Mustang, Ranger, Explorer, Transit, Expedition) list it with the other ratio codes; the causes are adaptive learning, the valve body and a migrating clutch cylinder sleeve. The 10R140 bulletin of 2021 does not mention it. Nissan's nine-speed Frontier and Titan set it with the MIL on; the repair check drives each gear 1–9 for at least 10 s in manual mode.

causes.label: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong

symptoms: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 9
Harsh or delayed shifts
Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 9 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07F7.title: Gear 10 Incorrect Ratio
P07F7.description: A ratio code compares input or turbine speed divided by output speed with the ratio of the commanded gear; a slipping clutch or the wrong gear trips it. Ford's summaries describe the check (over 30 rpm off for more than 1.8 s, three times) for gears 1–6 only; its 10-speed bulletins show gears 7–10 as P076F, P07D9, P07F6 and P07F7. P07F7 covers 10th gear, so in practice only ten-speed automatics. Ford's 10R80 lists it in all its ratio bulletins. On the 2020 Super Duty with the 10R140 a 2025 bulletin shows P07F7 alone, with the powertrain wrench lamp instead of the MIL and 10th gear locked out, caused by a migrating sleeve in a clutch cylinder that leaks; an earlier bulletin blames sticking main valve-body valves. GM's 10-speed reports through clutch valve codes instead.

causes.label: Clutch slipping or hydraulic leak (Ford 10R: migrating sleeve in the CDF clutch cylinder)
Shift adaptives wrong or not learned
Sticking valve in the valve body
Fluid level low or fluid degraded
Turbine or output speed sensor signal wrong

symptoms: Slipping or flaring engine speed in gear 10

Check engine or transmission warning lamp
Gear 10 locked out, higher rpm at cruise

P07F8.title: Stuck in Gear 9
P07F8.description: P07F8 means gear 9 cannot be disengaged: the transmission stays in 9th despite the command to leave it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. The family is documented only for 8th gear on eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes (Maserati MC20: P07D7 and P07D8; Corvette 2020–23: P07D8), where hydraulic actuators move shift forks under position monitoring. Nine- and ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford, GM and Nissan report faults in 9th gear as a ratio code (P07F6) or through solenoid and clutch valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.

causes.label: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
Fluid or filter contaminated

symptoms: Transmission stays in gear 9 and will not downshift
Weak take-off after stopping
Transmission warning, limp mode

P07F9.title: Unable to Engage Gear 9
P07F9.description: P07F9 means the transmission does not reach the commanded 9th gear – the counterpart to P07F8, where 9th cannot be left. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. 'Unable to Engage' is documented only for eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes, for example the 2020–23 Corvette (P07D8, MIL on, sticking solenoid from debris). Nine- and ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford, GM and Nissan report faults in 9th gear as a ratio code (P07F6) or through valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.

causes.label: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
Shift fork or synchronizer damaged

symptoms: Gear 9 skipped or never reached, higher rpm at cruise
Check engine and transmission warning lamp
Jerky shifts, possibly loss of one half of a dual-clutch gearbox

P07FA.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 9
P07FA.description: P07FA belongs to the series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA for 9, P07FD for 10): when leaving 9th gear, the transmission ends up in a gear other than the commanded target, or the shift out of 9th goes wrong. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Ten-speed users such as Ford's 10R family and GM's 10L report such faults through ratio or valve codes; Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code. Possible causes are a sticking shift or clutch valve, a worn or leaking clutch, or wrong adaptives.

causes.label: Shift or clutch valve sticking
Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
Shift adaptives wrong
Fluid level or condition

symptoms: Wrong gear or harsh downshift out of 9th
Transmission warning, possibly limp mode

P07FB.title: Stuck in Gear 10
P07FB.description: P07FB means gear 10 cannot be disengaged: the transmission stays in 10th despite the command to leave it. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. The family is documented only for 8th gear on eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes (Maserati MC20, Corvette 2020–23); no dual-clutch gearbox with ten gears and these codes is known. Ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford and GM report faults in 10th gear as a ratio code (P07F7, on Ford's 10R140 with 10th gear locked out) or through valve codes. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.

causes.label: Shift fork actuator or shift valve sticking (contamination)
System pressure low or unstable (mechatronic pressure valve)
Shift fork, synchronizer or gear damaged
Fluid or filter contaminated

symptoms: Transmission stays in gear 10 and will not downshift
Weak take-off after stopping
Transmission warning, limp mode

P07FC.title: Unable to Engage Gear 10
P07FC.description: P07FC means the transmission does not reach the commanded 10th gear – the counterpart to P07FB, where 10th cannot be left. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. 'Unable to Engage' is documented only for eight-speed dual-clutch gearboxes, for example the 2020–23 Corvette (P07D8). Ten-speed planetary automatics from Ford and GM report a missing 10th gear as a ratio code (P07F7) or through valve codes; Ford's 10R140 then locks out 10th. The description follows the J2012 scheme and CARB's functional check of transmission outputs.

causes.label: Sticking solenoid or shift valve in the mechatronic unit
System pressure too low or unstable
Adaptives lost or wrong after software or parts work
Shift fork or synchronizer damaged

symptoms: Gear 10 skipped or never reached, higher rpm at cruise
Check engine and transmission warning lamp
Jerky shifts, possibly loss of one half of a dual-clutch gearbox

P07FD.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 10
P07FD.description: P07FD closes the series 'Incorrect Shift from Gear N' (P07DC–P07E3 for gears 1–8, P07FA for 9): when leaving 10th gear, the transmission ends up in a gear other than the commanded target, or the shift out of 10th goes wrong. No manufacturer document available to us uses it. Ten-speed users such as Ford's 10R family and GM's 10L report such faults through ratio or valve codes; Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code. Possible causes are a sticking shift or clutch valve, a worn or leaking clutch, or wrong adaptives.

causes.label: Shift or clutch valve sticking
Worn clutch or hydraulic leak on the clutches involved
Shift adaptives wrong
Fluid level or condition

symptoms: Wrong gear or harsh downshift out of 10th
Transmission warning, possibly limp mode

P07FE.title: Stuck in Gear Not Specified
P07FE.description: P07FE is the catch-all of the 'Stuck in Gear' family: the transmission stays in a gear it was commanded to leave, but the module cannot or does not name the gear. The gear-specific codes are P072B–P073C for reverse and gears 1–7, P07D7 for 8th, P07F8 for 9th and P07FB for 10th. No manufacturer document available to us uses P07FE; the gear-specific codes are documented on dual-clutch gearboxes such as Ford's DPS6 and Maserati's MC20, whose actuators move shift drums or forks. Typical causes are a sticking shift actuator or valve, low or unstable system pressure, mechanical damage, or a faulty position or speed signal.

causes.label: Shift actuator or shift valve sticking
System pressure low or unstable
Mechanical damage in the gear train
Position or speed sensor signal wrong

symptoms: Transmission no longer shifts and stays in one gear
Limp mode, transmission warning

P07FF.title: Cold Start Transmission Performance
P07FF.description: P07FF means the transmission does not work as expected during the cold-start phase, shortly after starting with cold, thick fluid – for example a gear preselection or a clutch or valve response outside the expected window. The only documented user is Mercedes-Benz: its 2024 bulletin for the eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox 8G-DCT in the compact models (A-Class, CLA, GLA, GLB) names P07FF together with P0921, with reverse not available, a possible limp-home mode and the MIL; after switching off and on everything works again, and the fix was new control unit software. No thresholds or trip counts are published. It is not CARB's cold-start emission strategy, which concerns engine and catalyst heating (P050A ff), but a functional check of the transmission.

causes.label: Transmission control module software misjudging the cold phase
Shift valve or hydraulics too slow with cold fluid
Wrong or aged fluid, low level
Fluid temperature sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Reverse not available (message in the cluster)
Check engine lamp on
Limp-home mode shortly after a cold start
Normal again after switching off and on
